true_positives.matched_candidate:
Advanced negative-offset branch slices the queryset with a negative index, which Django rejects

When enable_advanced_features is set and the incoming cursor has a negative offset — trivially supplied by a client as cursor=0:-5:0, which Cursor.from_string parses without any validation — the branch at lines 877-882 executes queryset[cursor.offset : cursor.offset + limit + extra] with a negative start index. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing/slicing by raising ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."), so the comment claiming "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false and this request crashes with an unhandled 500. The endpoint in organization_auditlogs.py enables this path for superusers/global-access members who pass optimized_pagination=true, so any such caller supplying a negative-offset cursor gets a server error instead of the advertised "efficient reverse pagination."

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
organization_context.member may be None; unconditional .has_global_access dereference can 500 every audit log request

RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is Optional — it is None when the caller can access the organization without holding a membership, e.g. requests authenticated with an organization auth token, where request.user is anonymous and is_superuser is False. For those callers the short-circuit on request.user.is_superuser does not protect the second operand, and evaluating organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'. Because this line executes unconditionally for every GET (not only when optimized_pagination=true), it turns previously working requests into 500s. It should be guarded (e.g. organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access), and it should be verified that has_global_access exists on the RpcOrganizationMember pydantic model, not only on the ORM OrganizationMember.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator applies numeric key math to a datetime column and 500s on every non-empty page

The audit log endpoint invokes OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key and value_from_cursor were copied from the numeric Paginator instead of DateTimePaginator. get_item_key executes math.ceil(getattr(item, "datetime")), which raises TypeError ("must be real number, not datetime.datetime") because datetime objects have no float conversion. build_cursor calls get_item_key whenever a page has at least one result (to compute the next/prev cursor values), so any request with optimized_pagination=true against an organization that has at least one audit log entry fails with an unhandled 500. Even if that were fixed, value_from_cursor returns the raw millisecond cursor value, which build_queryset then compares directly against the timestamp column in SQL (datetime_col <= <bigint>) instead of converting it back to a datetime the way DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor does, so page 2 and beyond would return wrong data or a database error. The class should subclass DateTimePaginator or reuse its get_item_key/value_from_cursor implementations.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
Comment claims BasePaginator now allows negative offsets, but the code clamps them to 0

The added comment in BasePaginator.get_result says the change will "allow negative offsets to enable efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning," but the code does the opposite for forward cursors: start_offset = max(0, offset) clamps any negative offset to 0, and for previous-page cursors the behavior is identical to before (the offset is passed through unchanged). The change is therefore a behavior-preserving clamp, not the optimization described, and the misleading text (echoed by the comment added in cursors.py:26-27) may lead future callers to believe negative offsets are safely supported here, when any negative value that actually reaches a queryset slice raises ValueError.

New paginator and audit-log pagination path ship with no tests

The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator (about 90 lines duplicating BasePaginator.get_result) plus a new branch in the organization audit logs endpoint, but adds no tests for either. A single smoke test calling the endpoint with optimized_pagination=true against an org containing one audit log entry would have caught that get_item_key crashes on datetime values (paginator.py:840), and a negative-offset test would have caught the invalid queryset slicing (paginator.py:882). Since this paginator is documented as intended for reuse on high-traffic endpoints, it needs coverage for the first page, next/prev pages with datetime cursors, and negative offsets before merging.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
'Advanced' negative-offset pagination relies on Django negative slicing, which raises

The new branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (and the comments at paginator.py:179-181, 874-879 and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27) claims the Django ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' and that negative offsets are a safe, supported optimization. That is false: Django's QuerySet slicing raises ('Negative indexing is not supported') for queryset[start:stop] with start < 0. Cursor offsets are client-controlled — Cursor.from_string happily parses a cursor like '0:-50:0' — so with enable_advanced_features=True any client can supply a negative offset and get an unhandled 500, and the advertised bidirectional-pagination feature cannot work at all as written. The feature should be removed or implemented explicitly (e.g. computing absolute offsets), and the misleading comments in paginator.py and cursors.py corrected.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime keys, breaking the new audit-log pagination path

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), copying Paginator's numeric-key implementation. The only place it is wired up, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses it with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is 'datetime' and the attribute is a datetime.datetime; math.ceil(datetime_obj) raises TypeError. build_cursor calls get_item_key on results of every non-empty page, so every request with ?optimized_pagination=true from an eligible user (superuser or member with global access) returns a 500 as soon as the organization has any audit log rows. value_from_cursor also returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting epoch-millis back to a datetime like DateTimePaginator does, so even if the first page worked, subsequent pages would compare a datetime column against an integer. The 'optimized' path is completely broken as shipped; it needs DateTimePaginator-style key conversion (or should not be used on this endpoint). Note this endpoint/paginator change is also entirely unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (spans buffer eviction).

true_positives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
organization_context.member.has_global_access crashes when member is None, on every GET

Line 71 evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally for every request to the audit log endpoint. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is None when the request is not tied to an organization member — for example API-key or org-token authentication, where request.user is anonymous and is_superuser is False, so the 'or' short-circuit does not help. Such credentials can pass OrganizationAuditPermission via org scopes, and they will now crash with AttributeError ('NoneType' has no attribute 'has_global_access'), i.e. a 500 on this endpoint even when the optimized_pagination parameter is not used. Guard the access (organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access) and/or compute it lazily only when use_optimized is true.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.

false_positives.candidate:
No test covers the new 1000-span eviction during insert

The headline behavior of this PR — capping a segment's buffer at 1000 spans by ZPOPMIN-ing the lowest-scored (oldest) spans during insert — has no test coverage. The test changes only add the new required end_timestamp_precise field to Span constructors. Add a test that inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment (including the path where a child set is merged via ZUNIONSTORE) and asserts the buffer is capped at 1000 and that the evicted spans are the expected oldest ones.

Redirect-follow limit silently reduced 10000→1000 and its explanatory comment deleted

The redirect-chasing loop limit was lowered from 10000 to 1000, and the comment documenting the consequence ('theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly') was removed. Segment trees whose redirect chain exceeds 1000 will now silently stop resolving: the incoming span is written to its own buffer key and the trace is eventually flushed as multiple split segments with outcome 'different'. If the lower bound is an intentional tradeoff to bound Lua execution time, that decision and its correctness impact should stay documented in the script; otherwise restore the previous limit.

SET→ZSET type change on existing span-buf:s:* keys will WRONGTYPE during rollout

The PR changes the value type of the existing span-buf:s:* keys from a Redis SET (SADD here, SUNIONSTORE/SCARD/SSCAN elsewhere) to a sorted set (ZADD here, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE in add-buffer.lua, ZSCAN in _load_segment_data) without renaming the keys. Any buffer key that still exists as a SET when the new code deploys — segments not yet flushed, or orphaned keys with TTL up to redis_ttl (1h) — will cause WRONGTYPE errors in the ZADD pipeline, in the Lua script, and in the flusher's ZSCAN, making the consumer and the flusher error repeatedly on those traces until the old keys expire. Use a new versioned key prefix or otherwise migrate/flush the old keys as part of the deploy.

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, corrupting eviction scores for duplicated spans

Both ZUNIONSTORE calls omit an explicit AGGREGATE, so members present in both source sets get their scores SUMMED. With at-least-once Kafka delivery, a duplicate span payload can already be merged into set_key and later be re-buffered under a recreated child/parent key; the next merge then doubles its score (~3.4e9 instead of the ~1.7e9 end_timestamp_precise). Since the score is only used for eviction ordering, duplicated spans are subsequently treated as the newest spans and are evicted last by the 1000-span cap below, skewing eviction and, with repeated duplicates, crowding out legitimate spans. Add 'AGGREGATE MAX' (or MIN) to both ZUNIONSTORE calls so scores stay idempotent.

max_segment_spans is now dead configuration; Lua eviction hardcodes 1000

The only enforcement of the max_segment_spans constructor parameter (default 1001) — the span-count overflow check in _load_segment_data — was removed, and its replacement, the eviction in add-buffer.lua, hardcodes the threshold ('if span_count > 1000'). The configurable parameter no longer has any effect and even disagrees with the hardcoded value (1000 vs 1001). Either pass the limit into the Lua script as an argument or delete the now-misleading parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility check uses outer `dataset`/request query instead of the scoped dataset and effective query

Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` passes `dataset` — the closure variable chosen once in `get()` — instead of the `scoped_dataset` argument that is actually queried, and the helper's `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET['query']` rather than the `query` argument passed into `_get_event_stats`. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`), which only runs when the outer dataset is `metrics_performance`/`metrics_enhanced_performance`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` therefore always returns False, so the errors-only subquery (`(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction` run against the discover dataset) is never upsampled: allowlisted projects silently get raw counts instead of sample-weighted counts there. Conversely, any future caller that swaps `scoped_dataset` or rewrites `query` (the split path already does both) gets a transform decision computed against the wrong dataset and wrong query text. The check should use `scoped_dataset` and the effective `query`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental nested git submodule of the repo itself committed

This PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing a gitlink (`Subproject commit a5d29095...` — the base commit of this same repository) with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is clearly an accidental artifact of local testing: any checkout flow that initializes submodules will fail with `fatal: No url found for submodule path 'sentry-repo' in .gitmodules`, and the stray gitlink pollutes the tree. It should be removed from the commit.

Cache-invalidation helper is never called, so allowlist changes are stale for up to 60s with no escape hatch

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is added with a docstring saying it 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes', but nothing in this PR or elsewhere calls it — there is no hook on the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option. As shipped, edits to the allowlist take up to the 60-second cache TTL to take effect and there is no way to force invalidation, while the dead function implies an invalidation path that does not exist. Either wire it into the option-change path or remove it.

Substring match for 'event.type:error' also matches negations and quoted strings

`_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring test: `"event.type:error" in query`. This also matches negated filters such as `!event.type:error` (a query that explicitly excludes errors) and quoted search values like `message:"event.type:error"`, and it treats mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` as purely error-focused. For such discover queries on fully allowlisted projects, `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` (sum of sample_weight) even though the result set contains non-error events that have no sample_weight, so the returned counts are NULL or undercounted relative to the real totals. The check should parse the query or at minimum reject matches that are negated or inside quotes.

upsampled_count drops rows with NULL sample_weight, silently undercounting

The new `upsampled_count` aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. ClickHouse `sum()` ignores NULLs, so any error row whose `sample_weight` is NULL contributes nothing at all — not even 1. That covers errors ingested before a project was added to the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` (still inside retention) and errors stored without an `error_sampling.client_sample_rate` context — the PR's own test-factory change only sets `sample_rate` when that context is present, demonstrating such rows exist. The result is that upsampled counts for allowlisted projects can be lower than the true event count, with no indication to the user. Wrapping the column, e.g. `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`, would make unsampled rows count as 1.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
zip(error_ids, events.values()) mis-pairs error IDs with event data from nodestore get_multi

`fetch_error_details` builds `ErrorEvent` objects with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id whose value order is whatever the backend returned (the Django backend uses an unordered `id__in` query, effectively lexicographic by node id, not the input order), and it omits entries for ids that have no stored event. As a result the i-th `error_id` is not guaranteed to correspond to the i-th value: titles, messages and timestamps get attached to the wrong error ids, and any single missing event shifts every subsequent pairing. The corrupted records are then sorted by the wrong `timestamp` and sent to Seer as the error context for the replay summary, so the summary can cite the wrong errors in the wrong chronological positions. The function already computes `node_ids`; it should look up each event explicitly (e.g. `events.get(node_id)` for each `(error_id, node_id)` pair) instead of relying on `.values()` ordering.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty columns and data

In `tableResultComponent`, the `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{ data: [], meta: { fields: {}, units: {} } }} />` — literal empty columns and empty data — while ignoring the real query results (`result.data`, `fields`, `result.meta`, `fieldAliases`) that are computed immediately above and still feed the `StyledSimpleTableChart` fallback. As soon as the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag is turned on for an organization, every table widget on that organization's dashboards renders an empty table with no headers and no rows. This reads as an unfinished stub that slipped in: either wire the actual table results into `TableWidgetVisualization` or keep rendering `StyledSimpleTableChart` until the new path is implemented.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators bypassable with a 0 value

`validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` are meant to enforce that a report contains either `age` (Editor's Draft) or `timestamp` (Working Draft), never both, but they check presence via truthiness: `if self.initial_data.get("age")` / `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A report containing both fields passes validation whenever one of them is `0` (e.g. `age: 0` alongside a `timestamp`), because `0` is falsy, defeating the mutual-exclusion rule the endpoint explicitly documents in the serializer comments. Use a real presence check such as `"age" in self.initial_data` (or `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None`) so zero values cannot bypass the constraint.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
"Project not found" error flashes while projects are still loading

The new guard `if (replayRecord?.project_id && !project)` renders an error alert ("Project not found. Unable to load AI summary.") whenever `useProjectFromId` returns undefined. However `useProjectFromId` also returns undefined while the projects store is still loading, so on any visit where projects are not already cached the user briefly (or, on a slow load, persistently) sees a false error state instead of the loading spinner that the previous code fell through to. The error branch should be gated on the projects store having finished loading (e.g. check `initiallyLoaded` from `useProjects`) so it only fires when the project genuinely cannot be found.

Merged-PR comment helpers defined on CommitContextIntegration but called on PRCommentWorkflow, causing AttributeError

The new static method `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `_truncate_title` (along with `get_environment_info` and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` themselves) is added at the end of `CommitContextIntegration` — the diff places them immediately after `get_top_5_issues_by_count` and immediately before `class OpenPRCommentWorkflow(ABC):`. `PRCommentWorkflow` is a separate ABC that only composes an integration (`__init__(self, integration: CommitContextIntegration)`), so `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` does not exist and raises AttributeError the first time a merged-PR comment body is formatted. The same mismatch exists at the call sites: `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` now invoke `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` and `self.get_environment_info(...)` on workflow instances that do not inherit from `CommitContextIntegration`. Consequence: the merged-PR suspect-issues comment tasks for GitHub and GitLab crash instead of posting/updating the comment. Move the helpers onto `PRCommentWorkflow` (and fix the class referenced in the static call), or invoke them via `self.integration`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code verification and consumption are not atomic

The authorize flow decrypts the stored codes, checks `indexOf`, and then issues a separate `prisma.user.update` to persist the remaining codes. Two concurrent login requests presenting the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update commits, so a nominally single-use code can be redeemed twice within the race window. Consider consuming the code atomically (e.g., in a transaction with a re-read/optimistic check) or documenting acceptance of the risk.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
A backup code plus any arbitrary non-empty totpCode bypasses password verification

In the credentials authorize() flow, the password check above (lines 121-129) only runs when `!credentials.totpCode`. The new backup-code branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` runs regardless of whether the password was ever verified. An attacker who knows a victim's email and one backup code (a static 10-hex-character secret, e.g. from the downloadable cal-backup-codes.txt) can log in by submitting email + backupCode + any dummy non-empty totpCode such as "000000": the presence of totpCode makes the password-verification condition false, and the backup-code branch then authenticates them and creates a session. Backup codes are intended as a second factor in addition to the password; this makes one static factor alone sufficient for account takeover. The skip exists to support the IdP totp redirect flow, but the backup-code branch should require successful password verification for CAL (password) users, or the password check should not be conditioned on totpCode being absent.

Backup codes cannot be used by Google/SAML users in the IdP two-factor challenge

When a Google/SAML user with 2FA signs in, they are redirected to /auth/login?totp=<jwt>, which renders the TOTP input with `ExternalTotpFooter` — only a Cancel button, no "Lost access" option — so there is no way in the UI to enter a backup code. A backup-code-only request is also rejected server-side: in next-auth-options.ts the guards `user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode` (lines 113-121) throw ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled / IncorrectEmailPassword before the new backup-code branch is reached. Consequence: identity-provider users who lose their authenticator remain locked out despite having valid backup codes; the recovery feature only works for CAL password accounts.

Consumed backup codes are nulled in place instead of removed

After a successful backup-code login, `backupCodes[index] = null` is persisted rather than splicing the used code out of the array. The stored JSON keeps accumulating null placeholders, `user.backupCodes` stays truthy forever, and once all 10 codes have been used the user gets `IncorrectBackupCode` instead of an indication that their codes are exhausted (`MissingBackupCodes` only fires when codes were never generated). Splice the redeemed code out and treat an empty array the same as having no backup codes.

First 2FA e2e test not updated for the new backup-code screen; its assertion is admittedly broken

In "should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA", after the OTP is accepted the modal now displays the backup-codes screen, but the test never interacts with it or closes it (unlike the second test, which was updated). The subsequent check on the switch state is annotated with a newly added FIXME stating it passes even when the switch is not checked, and since `onEnable` now only fires from the backup-codes Close button, the enabled state is never confirmed. This test would stay green even if enabling 2FA regressed. It should close the backup-code screen and assert on `data-state="checked"` like the second test does.

No test covers logging in with a backup code or its one-time-use guarantee

The security-critical behavior introduced by this PR — authenticating with a backup code, rejecting an invalid code, and consuming a code so it cannot be reused — has no automated coverage. The added test code only checks the download filename and the copy toast, and a TODO acknowledges the missing tests. A regression making backup codes reusable, unconsumed, or rejected would ship undetected.

missing_backup_codes message instructs users to do something impossible

The new string "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." is shown on the login page when a user with 2FA enabled but no backup codes uses the "Lost access" flow — i.e., users who enabled 2FA before this feature existed and are now locked out of their authenticator. There is no settings UI to (re)generate backup codes for an account that already has 2FA enabled (codes are only created during initial setup), and a locked-out user cannot reach settings anyway. The recovery instruction cannot be followed and will generate support tickets.

navigator.clipboard used without an availability check

The Copy button calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` directly. The Clipboard API is only exposed in secure contexts; on self-hosted instances served over plain HTTP, `navigator.clipboard` is undefined, so clicking Copy throws a TypeError and the user gets no feedback at all (the success toast is never reached). Feature-detect `navigator.clipboard` and fall back to a hidden-textarea copy, or show an error toast.

onEnable only fires from the backup-codes Close button, leaving stale state on other dismiss paths

Before this change, `onEnable()` (which makes the parent settings page refresh and show the 2FA switch as enabled) ran immediately when /api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable returned 200. It is now replaced with `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and only called from the "Close" button on the backup-codes screen. If the user dismisses the dialog any other way — the dialog's X button, Escape key, or overlay click, all routed through `onOpenChange` — `onEnable()` never runs, so the settings page keeps showing 2FA as disabled even though it is now on (until a manual refetch), and `resetState()` also doesn't run, so reopening the modal lands on the stale backup-codes screen displaying the old codes. The parent notification/state reset should happen on any close of the final step, not just the Close button.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent fallback for missing externalCalendarId is dead code; updates fail with calendarId undefined

In `updateEvent`, the new fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That `.find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares each calendar's `externalId` against `null`/`""` and can never match — `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined` in that case, and `calendar.events.update` is then called with `calendarId: undefined`, which throws and leaves the Google event un-updated (caught upstream as success=false, so the booking is rescheduled in cal.com but the calendar event keeps the old time). The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. This matters more now because other changes in this PR create references with `externalCalendarId: null` (see EventManager updateLocation and the no-credentialId create branch). The same dead `.find` pattern exists in `deleteEvent` (line 315-317), where it is only masked by the later `calendarId ? calendarId : "primary"` fallback.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for org slug is inverted

This PR (which is about destination calendars) changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting the condition. Previously, when team billing was disabled (e.g. self-hosted), the org got its `slug` immediately, and when billing was enabled only `requestedSlug` was stored so the real slug could be set after payment. After this change, billing-enabled installs set `slug` before payment (bypassing the paid flow) and billing-disabled installs never set a slug at all, leaving the organization without a usable URL. This looks like an accidental flip during an unrelated edit and should be reverted.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
CalDAV createEvent silently reports success without creating anything for other hosts

The CalDAV base service filters `calendars` to `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. When EventManager creates the event for a non-organizer host's CalDAV credential (collective events), that host's account does not contain the main host's calendar URL, so the filtered list is empty, `Promise.all([])` resolves to `[]`, `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is false, and the method returns a successful result with a uid — but no event was created anywhere. This is a silent data-integrity failure: the booking reference is stored, but the team member's calendar has no event. It should match the destination calendar for the credential in use, like Google's credentialId lookup.

Dynamic user query no longer selects organization

The `loadUsers` refactor rewrote the dynamic-group user lookup and dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the `prisma.user.findMany` select (it was explicitly selected before, together with `metadata`). Any downstream code for dynamic collective bookings that reads `user.organization.slug` (e.g. org-subdomain/booker-url handling) will now get `undefined` and potentially throw. This removal is unrelated to the destination-calendar change and looks accidental; it should be restored.

Google Meet fallback crashes when booking has no destination calendar

In `create()`, the code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. When the event has no destination calendar (`null` from handleNewBooking, or `[]` from confirm/payment flows), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError. This is exactly the scenario this branch exists for ("Fallback to Cal Video if Google Meet is selected w/o a Google Cal"), so any booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar now crashes instead of falling back to Daily. The old code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`); this needs `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Hangout-link patch call uses possibly-undefined calendarId

In `createEvent`, the insert call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (that writes the description with the hangout link) passes the raw `selectedCalendar`, which is `undefined` whenever no destination calendar matches the credentialId. The google client will throw a missing-parameter error for that patch, so the hangout link is never written into the event description in that case. Previously `selectedCalendar` was always defined (defaulted to "primary").

Lark createEvent uses the first destination calendar regardless of which host's credential is used

Same class of bug as the Office365 service: `createEvent` derives `calendarId` from `event.destinationCalendar[0]` (the main host's calendar). For collective bookings, EventManager invokes `createEvent` separately for each host's credential, but Lark will always attempt `POST /calendar/v4/calendars/{mainHostCalendarId}/events/create_event` with the team member's token, which the member has no access to — so non-organizer hosts never get Lark calendar events. The service should select the destination calendar matching the credential being used (as the Google service now does with the credentialId parameter).

No automated tests cover the new multi-destination calendar logic

The PR rewrites `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` and the create/update/delete paths of four calendar providers for the collective multi-host scenario, but the author explicitly checked "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective". The only test change is a webhook payload expectation. Regressions introduced here (e.g. the Google Meet fallback TypeError, non-Google providers writing to the main host's calendar, video references losing credentialId) would be caught by even a minimal unit test around `EventManager.create` with multiple destination calendars.

Office365 createEvent always targets the main host's calendar, even when creating for another host

`createEvent` now takes the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` (`mainHostDestinationCalendar`) and posts to `/me/calendars/{mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`. For collective events, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` calls `createEvent` once per host with that host's credential, but the full event (with all destination calendars, main host first) is passed each time. So when creating the event for a non-organizer host's Office365 account, it tries to write to the main host's calendar id using the team member's token, which fails (404/403) — the team member never gets the event. `CalendarManager.createEvent` already receives the per-destination `externalId` but doesn't forward it to `calendar.createEvent`; the credentialId-based lookup used in the Google service (or forwarding externalId) is needed here too.

Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging bookings on reschedule

When `newBookingId` is set (reschedule/merge path), the code deletes the old booking's calendar event via `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))`. Bookings can now have multiple calendar references (one per collective host), so only the first host's old event is deleted; the other hosts keep a stale event at the old time. This should iterate over all calendar references of the old booking.

Recurring-event deletion block now runs once per calendar reference

The recurring-cancellation branch (mapping over all of the organizer's calendar credentials × all updated recurring bookings and deleting each) lives inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With multiple calendar references (the collective multi-host case this PR introduces, typically one per host), the entire recurring deletion pass executes once per reference, issuing duplicate `deleteEvent` calls for the same events. Google tolerates this via 404/410 handling, but other providers may log errors and it doubles the external API traffic. The recurring branch should run once, outside the per-reference loop. (Separately, that branch still only deletes the first calendar reference per updated booking, so team-member calendar events for recurring collective bookings remain stale.)

Team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer and event type have none

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and the collective-team calendars are added via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Optional chaining means that when the base value is `null`, the push is silently skipped: for a collective event where the organizer has no connected destination calendar but team members do, none of the team members' calendars receive events (and the booking's destinationCalendar is not connected either). The array should be initialized to `[]` (or the team calendars assigned directly) so collective hosts still get their events.

Video booking references lose credentialId, breaking meeting deletion on cancel

In `create()`'s `referencesToCreate`, the credentialId is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously it was `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, i.e. video results kept `result.credentialId` from `createMeeting`. With this change, every newly created video BookingReference is stored with `credentialId: null`. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (it looks up the credential by id to call `deleteMeeting`), so cancelling bookings created after this change will leave orphaned Zoom/Daily/etc. meetings that are never deleted. There is no reason to special-case calendar types here; use `result.credentialId` for all results.

Webhook payload sends destinationCalendar as null in some flows and [] in others

The updated e2e expectations now encode that BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED payloads contain `destinationCalendar: null` while BOOKING_REJECTED contains `destinationCalendar: []` — because handleNewBooking emits `null` when there is no destination calendar while confirm.handler emits `[]`. This is an inconsistent contract for the same field across webhook triggers, and the field's shape also changed from a single object to an array, which is a breaking change for existing webhook consumers despite the PR being labelled non-breaking. Consider normalizing (always array, or always null-when-empty) across all emitters.

updateLocation references are created without credentialId/externalCalendarId

`updateLocation()` now builds references with `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`, but the calendar-update results come from `updateAllCalendarEvents` → `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, whose returned EventResult never sets `externalId` or `credentialId`. Both fields are therefore always `undefined`, and `editLocation.handler` persists these references on the booking (`references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`). The old code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` / `?.credentialId`. Consequence: bookings that go through "edit location" accumulate calendar references with no credential/calendar linkage, so later updates/deletes can't find the right credential and fall into legacy paths (including the broken Google `updateEvent` fallback).

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema is not valid zod: it strips everything except access_token and forces refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token"

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` do not create a catch-all (they evaluate to a fixed string such as "[object Object]"), and z.object strips unknown keys by default. So in sync mode the parse result contains only `access_token`; any expiry field returned by the sync endpoint is dropped, and lines 25-27 then set `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token". Consequences downstream: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 264 spreads this over the stored credentials, overwriting the user's real refresh token with "refresh_token" in the DB; zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000` where expires_in was stripped, storing NaN and also persisting the placeholder refresh token. Use z.catchall/passthrough for the permissive schema and preserve real expiry/refresh-token data.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zod SafeParse wrapper object is stored as the credential key, corrupting Google credentials on every refresh

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result object ({ success: true, data: {...} }), but line 97-100 stores that whole wrapper as the credential key: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Before this PR the key was the plain parsed token object. After the first access-token refresh, credential.key in the DB becomes {"success":true,"data":{...tokens...}}, and the next time GoogleCalendarService is constructed `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws because the tokens are nested under `data`. This breaks Google Calendar for every user whose token refreshes, on default (non-sync) installs too. Extract `.data` (or change the helper to return parsed data) before persisting.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync-mode returns a raw fetch Response but several callers expect parsed/library-specific shapes

In sync mode this helper returns the unparsed fetch Response, but multiple integrations handle the return value as if it were the library-specific response: googlecalendar reads `res?.data` (a fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token.access_token` throws a TypeError that is swallowed by the catch and the expired token is silently reused); hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts treats it as HubspotToken (`expiresIn` is undefined so expiryDate becomes NaN, `setAccessToken(undefined)` is called, and the Response object itself is persisted as the credential key); zohocrm and zoho-bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error`, throwing TypeError since `.data` is undefined. Credential sync mode is therefore broken (or corrupts stored credentials) for google-calendar, hubspot, zohocrm and zoho-bigin. The helper should parse the JSON body and normalize the response shape, or callers must be adapted.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
