false_positives.candidate:
SET→ZSET type change on existing span-buf:s:* keys will WRONGTYPE during rollout

The PR changes the value type of the existing span-buf:s:* keys from a Redis SET (SADD here, SUNIONSTORE/SCARD/SSCAN elsewhere) to a sorted set (ZADD here, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE in add-buffer.lua, ZSCAN in _load_segment_data) without renaming the keys. Any buffer key that still exists as a SET when the new code deploys — segments not yet flushed, or orphaned keys with TTL up to redis_ttl (1h) — will cause WRONGTYPE errors in the ZADD pipeline, in the Lua script, and in the flusher's ZSCAN, making the consumer and the flusher error repeatedly on those traces until the old keys expire. Use a new versioned key prefix or otherwise migrate/flush the old keys as part of the deploy.

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, corrupting eviction scores for duplicated spans

Both ZUNIONSTORE calls omit an explicit AGGREGATE, so members present in both source sets get their scores SUMMED. With at-least-once Kafka delivery, a duplicate span payload can already be merged into set_key and later be re-buffered under a recreated child/parent key; the next merge then doubles its score (~3.4e9 instead of the ~1.7e9 end_timestamp_precise). Since the score is only used for eviction ordering, duplicated spans are subsequently treated as the newest spans and are evicted last by the 1000-span cap below, skewing eviction and, with repeated duplicates, crowding out legitimate spans. Add 'AGGREGATE MAX' (or MIN) to both ZUNIONSTORE calls so scores stay idempotent.

Redirect-follow limit silently reduced 10000→1000 and its explanatory comment deleted

The redirect-chasing loop limit was lowered from 10000 to 1000, and the comment documenting the consequence ('theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly') was removed. Segment trees whose redirect chain exceeds 1000 will now silently stop resolving: the incoming span is written to its own buffer key and the trace is eventually flushed as multiple split segments with outcome 'different'. If the lower bound is an intentional tradeoff to bound Lua execution time, that decision and its correctness impact should stay documented in the script; otherwise restore the previous limit.

max_segment_spans is now dead configuration; Lua eviction hardcodes 1000

The only enforcement of the max_segment_spans constructor parameter (default 1001) — the span-count overflow check in _load_segment_data — was removed, and its replacement, the eviction in add-buffer.lua, hardcodes the threshold ('if span_count > 1000'). The configurable parameter no longer has any effect and even disagrees with the hardcoded value (1000 vs 1001). Either pass the limit into the Lua script as an argument or delete the now-misleading parameter.

No test covers the new 1000-span eviction during insert

The headline behavior of this PR — capping a segment's buffer at 1000 spans by ZPOPMIN-ing the lowest-scored (oldest) spans during insert — has no test coverage. The test changes only add the new required end_timestamp_precise field to Span constructors. Add a test that inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment (including the path where a child set is merged via ZUNIONSTORE) and asserts the buffer is capped at 1000 and that the evicted spans are the expected oldest ones.

false_positives.candidate:
Stale denial-cache entry overrides fresher permission data already in the server's cache

In Service.Check, the permission-denial cache is consulted first and short-circuits the request, before the permission cache is checked for an allow. A denial entry is written only after a fresh DB lookup denies, but it then lives for shortCacheTTL (30s). Meanwhile, any DB re-query for the same user+action (triggered by a check on a different resource, or by cache expiry) rewrites the entire permCache scope map with fresh permissions, because getUserPermissions always calls permCache.Set after fetching. Concrete sequence: t0 Check(user, dashboards:read, dash1) denies and caches a denial for dash1; t1 the user is granted access to dash1 and dash2; t2 Check(user, dashboards:read, dash2) misses the cached scope map, re-queries the DB, allows, and repopulates permCache with permissions that now include dash1; t3 Check(user, dashboards:read, dash1) hits the stale denial entry and returns Allowed=false even though the server's own permission cache (and the DB) would allow it. The user stays denied for that resource until the denial entry expires. This partially undermines the PR's stated goal (a single check that races the permission write poisons the resource for 30s). Checking the permission cache for an allow before consulting the denial cache would preserve the fast-deny path while preventing stale denials from overriding fresher allow data the server already holds.

This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.

false_positives.candidate:
Network/API failures during token exchange and /user fetch are unhandled and produce 500s

OAuthLoginView.dispatch performs two outbound HTTP calls that can raise: `req = safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` (line 423) is outside the try/except (the try only covers safe_urlread/parsing), and `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) has no exception handling at all. On deployments that have the GitHub App configured but never set up the github-login identity provider (a plausible self-hosted configuration), these values are None/empty: the pipeline will redirect to GitHub's authorize URL with an invalid client_id (GitHub shows an error) or the token exchange will fail, making the GitHub integration uninstallable where it previously worked. There is no feature flag, fallback, or documentation noting this new requirement. Consider gating the new step on the OAuth app being configured, or explicitly failing with a clear operator-facing error/docs update.

The new tests only cover the negative case (test_github_user_mismatch: webhook-created Integration whose sender does not match the OAuth user). There is no test that exercises the main protected flow end-to-end: installation webhook creates the Integration with a sender, the same GitHub user completes the OAuth step, the sender check passes, and the installation links successfully (the direct-from-GitHub install path). A regression that breaks legitimate installs from GitHub would not be caught. There is also no test with a pre-existing ACTIVE Integration whose metadata lacks `sender`, which would have exposed the KeyError in `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` reported separately.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. Because there is no second check after the write lock is acquired, any requests that arrive concurrently before the cache is first populated will each perform the full manifest load sequentially and overwrite each other's cache entry. Besides duplicated disk I/O, a transient read error in a later goroutine can replace an already-populated good cache entry with nil and return an error to its caller even though a valid cached value existed. The standard fix is to re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after taking the write lock.

On other databases the batch size is configurable and unvalidated: if it is set above the driver's bind-parameter cap (65535 for Postgres, and MySQL prepared statements have a similar 65535 placeholder limit), every cleanup batch will fail with a parameter-count error, so cleanup never makes progress. With the batch size this path is designed for (e.g. 32767 IDs, as exercised by the new test), that is on the order of gigabytes of byte copying per batch, repeated on every cleanup cycle while a backlog exists. Using a strings.Builder with strconv.AppendInt (or strings.Join on pre-formatted values) would make it linear.

In the Kubernetes API server the request context is canceled as soon as the HTTP handler returns, which happens immediately after the synchronous unified-storage write completes. The detached goroutine therefore almost always executes with an already-canceled context and the legacy write fails with 'context canceled' — in mode 3 the legacy copy (the stated 'safe measure') is silently skipped, with only a metric recording the failure. With the new code, create-on-update paths that generate names/UIDs produce different objects in legacy vs unified storage, and any mutating logic inside UpdatedObject runs twice, so the two stores can silently hold divergent objects — exactly what dual write is meant to prevent. The object should be materialized once and the frozen result passed to the legacy update via updateWrapper, as before.

The diff removes the alertRuleApi prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...) dispatch but leaves the comment 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX. Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded' and the variable name cacheAndRulerPreload. The comment now describes behavior that no longer exists and is misleading about what the remaining upsertQueryData does; update the comment and rename the variable.

Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting defeats the $__range no-splitting guard

runSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (line 299) before partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query)) runs on the next line. applyTemplateVariables substitutes the built-in range variables ($__range, $__range_s, $__range_ms) from scopedVars, and dashboard/Explore requests always carry those scoped vars. querySupportsSplitting() decides a query must not be split by calling isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr), which searches for the literal text '$__range' — but by the time it runs, that text has already been replaced (e.g. count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) has become count_over_time({a="b"}[30d])). Besides contradicting the documented intent, this is a real cost/correctness regression for large ranges: with a 30-day dashboard, each 1-day chunk evaluates count_over_time(...[30d]), re-scanning ~30 days of data per chunk (~30x the scanned volume of the previous single request). The existing unit tests do not catch this because the test requests carry no scopedVars, so $__range survives interpolation in tests but not in production. One of the interpolation layers should be removed (or the later passes skipped for already-interpolated targets).

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Under concurrent anonymous traffic (e.g., a public dashboard link being opened by many clients at once, or multiple Grafana HA replicas), the limit is only a soft cap. Consider enforcing the limit atomically (e.g., a single statement with a subquery guard, a transaction with appropriate isolation, or an INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit).

false_positives.candidate:
Translation LRU cache key ignores the site-specific fallback locale

The cache key for memoized translations is built only from the key, the current locale and the backend object id (`k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`). With this PR, the resolved value of a translation now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (via `FallbackLocaleList`), and that setting is per-site on multisite installs and can be changed at runtime — but it is not part of the cache key, and the cache itself (`@cache` on the I18n singleton) is process-global. Consequences: (1) on a multisite cluster sharing one process, a key missing in locale X is resolved through whichever site's default locale populated the cache first — e.g. a user on a site whose default is German can be served the French fallback string cached for another site, until the 300-entry LRU happens to evict it; (2) on a single site, after an admin changes `default_locale`, fallback strings in the old language keep being served from the cache until eviction. Previously (`config.i18n.fallbacks = true`) the fallback target was the global `I18n.default_locale`, so cached entries were consistent. Include `SiteSetting.default_locale` (or the resolved fallback chain) in the cache key, or clear `I18n`'s cache when the setting changes.

Fallback locale files are only loaded for controller requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers/rake

`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from the `set_locale` before_filter, i.e. only for HTTP requests through ApplicationController. The translate accelerator's `translate` only ever loads yml files for `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale)`); it never loads the fallback locales itself. Any server-side code that translates outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer views, rake tasks, console — with `I18n.locale` set to a non-English locale will walk the fallback chain (locale → site default → :en), find that no translations were ever loaded for the fallback locales, and render "translation missing: xx.yyy" instead of the site-default/English string. So the feature this PR adds silently does not work in exactly the server-side contexts that don't pass through a controller. Load the fallback locales inside the accelerator instead (e.g. have `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`translate` load every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`), or route jobs/mailers through the same ensure_loaded! step.

FallbackLocaleList#[] does a SiteSetting read and several array allocations on every interpolated translation

The i18n fallbacks backend calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every backend lookup, and `FallbackLocaleList#[]` performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read plus `[locale, ...].uniq.compact` (multiple array allocations) each time. The translate accelerator only memoizes argument-free lookups — every `I18n.t` call with interpolation options (the common case in this codebase, e.g. anything with `count:` or a username) bypasses the LRU cache and pays this cost per call, in a code path that exists specifically to make translation fast. Consider memoizing the computed list keyed by (locale, default_locale) and invalidating when the setting changes.

No tests for the new fallback semantics, which now apply to all environments

This PR rewrites how fallbacks are computed (new `FallbackLocaleList`, new `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, per-request `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`) and, as a side effect, enables fallbacks in every environment — previously they were only turned on via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in the production-like configs, so in development/test a key present in English but missing in the active locale now silently renders the English text instead of a "translation missing" message. No specs cover any of this. At minimum, add coverage that `I18n.fallbacks[:xx]` returns `[xx, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq`, that a key missing in the active locale resolves through the site default and then English, and that the fallback locale files are actually loaded (the `ensure_loaded!` path).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
traceID field dropped from "Plugin Request Completed" log lines

Before this change, LoggerMiddleware explicitly appended a "traceID" field to every "Plugin Request Completed" log line via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). This PR removes that code (and the tracing import) and relies entirely on contextual attributes attached by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware — but instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname; it never adds traceID. Nothing else in the plugin client middleware chain attaches traceID via log.WithContextualAttributes, so these log lines lose the trace ID whenever an upstream HTTP middleware hasn't already put it into the context — e.g. plugin calls originating from background services such as alerting evaluations, where the trace exists only as a span in ctx. This breaks log-to-trace correlation that previously always worked. Fix by either keeping the explicit traceID param in LoggerMiddleware or adding traceID inside instrumentContext.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies the exact same problem described in the golden comment: the removal of traceID extraction in LoggerMiddleware and its omission in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, resulting in missing traceIDs in plugin request logs.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh instance, so logs via FromContext are never recorded

TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(). This matters because the production code changed in this PR (LoggerMiddleware) now logs exclusively through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). Any test that injects a *TestLogger and then asserts on InfoLogs/ErrorLogs/etc. of the instance it holds will see zero recorded calls — tests expecting a log will fail confusingly, and tests asserting that nothing was logged will silently false-pass even though the code under test did log. The fake should return f (or record into shared state) so that logs written through FromContext are observable by the test.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same bug as the golden comment: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a new instance (`NewTestLogger()`) instead of the receiver `f`, causing logs made via `FromContext` to be unrecorded on the original instance used in test assertions.

false_positives.candidate:
LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier in the chain

LoggerMiddleware previously built the pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, and dsUID log fields itself from req.PluginContext, so it was self-contained. After this change those fields only appear if ContextualLoggerMiddleware ran earlier in the middleware stack and attached them as contextual attributes. The production wiring in CreateMiddlewares happens to order them correctly, but NewLoggerMiddleware is exported and can be composed into other middleware stacks (tests, other decorator constructions); in any stack without ContextualLoggerMiddleware ahead of it, the "Plugin Request Completed" lines lose all plugin-identifying fields with no error or warning. At minimum the ordering requirement should be documented on NewLoggerMiddleware (the old InstrumentationMiddleware had such a comment, and it was removed in the rename).

New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test, and no test covers the moved log fields

The PR adds a new middleware (ContextualLoggerMiddleware) responsible for attaching endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname to the request context, but adds no test verifying those attributes are attached, and the renamed metrics_middleware_test.go only covers the prometheus metrics. There is also no test asserting that LoggerMiddleware's "Plugin Request Completed" output still contains the fields that were moved out of it — which is exactly why the traceID regression introduced by this PR (the explicit traceID field was removed and is no longer added anywhere in the chain) is not caught by the test suite. A small test chaining ContextualLoggerMiddleware + LoggerMiddleware and asserting the resulting log fields would lock in the intended behavior.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil

The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is nil (e.g. an API call to POST /admin/embeddable_hosts without a host value), this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `self.host = self.host.to_s` or skip the substitutions when host is blank.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: the `before_validation` callback in the `EmbeddableHost` model calls `self.host.sub!`, which will raise a `NoMethodError` if `self.host` is nil.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy 500 on unknown id instead of 404

`update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking the result. For a stale or invalid id (e.g. two admins, one deletes a host while the other's page still shows it), `save_host(nil)` calls `nil.host = ...` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, both raising NoMethodError → 500. Additionally `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without verifying the wrapper param exists, so any request missing the `embeddable_host` key also 500s. Raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record doesn't exist and guard the params.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same bug as the golden comment: `update` and `destroy` call `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking if the result is nil, leading to a `NoMethodError` in `save_host` or `destroy` when an unknown ID is passed.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hosts saved with a port can never match; input host not downcased for comparison

The format validation explicitly allows a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but keeps the port, so an admin can save `example.com:3000`. But `record_for_host` compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` — `uri.host` never includes the port — so that row can never match any referer and the site silently can never embed. Also the bound value isn't downcased, so a mixed-case referer host won't match `lower(host)`. Either reject/normalize ports on save or include the port (and downcase the input) in the lookup.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly identifies the exact same bug as the golden comment (in addition to a port-handling issue): that `record_for_host` compares against `lower(host)` without downcasing the bound parameter (`uri.host`), causing mixed-case referer hosts to fail to match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted verbatim and will never match lookups

The old `embeddable_hosts` setting supported entries with scheme and path (e.g. `http://discourse.org`, `https://example.com/1234`) — the removed specs in site_setting_spec.rb and embed_controller_spec.rb prove these worked, because the old code compared against `URI(h).host`. The migration inserts the raw setting values into the new table, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` looks up `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, so any migrated row containing a scheme or path will never match a referer. After upgrading, previously working embedded comments silently stop working for those sites. The migration should normalize hosts the same way the model's `before_validation` does (strip scheme and path) or insert via the model.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue describe the exact same bug: the migration inserts `embeddable_hosts` values verbatim without normalizing them (stripping scheme like http/https and path segments), which causes the new bare-host lookup in `EmbeddableHost` to fail for migrated data.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents were swapped

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) that were deleted from the category file. The suite still passes only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory regardless of name, but the filenames are now actively misleading and the contents should be swapped back.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same problem: the contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` were accidentally swapped.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host values are interpolated into SQL without escaping

The INSERT interpolates the setting value directly: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. A value containing a single quote (legacy/malformed data in the old free-text setting) will produce invalid SQL and abort the migration. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize`/`quote` or a parameterized insert.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same problem: direct string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) into a SQL query without escaping/parameterization, and both recommend using parameter binding or proper quoting to fix it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when the embed_category site setting row is missing or matches no category

The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. The `embed_category` setting defaulted to an empty string and is only persisted in `site_settings` if an admin actually changed it, so on most installs (and any fresh DB) the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking the upgrade. It also crashes if the setting was set to a value that doesn't match a category name exactly. The same pattern at line 15 crashes if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Both lookups need nil-safe handling before indexing into the result.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: the migration directly accesses `execute(...)[0]['id']` when querying for `embed_category` without checking if any rows were returned, which causes a crash (nil error) when no `embed_category` setting exists.

false_positives.candidate:
embed_category is deleted even when no host rows were created

If a site used feed polling with `embed_category` set but had no `embeddable_hosts` configured (feed-only embedding, which previously worked because `TopicEmbed.import` used the global `SiteSetting.embed_category`), this migration creates zero `embeddable_hosts` rows and still deletes the `embed_category` setting. From then on `TopicEmbed.import` uses `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which finds nothing, so imported topics fall back to the uncategorized category — or fail validation entirely when `allow_uncategorized_topics` is false and the embedding user isn't staff. The previously configured category assignment is lost with no replacement.

Migration is not reversible despite using `change`

The migration uses `def change` but contains raw `execute` statements (data copy and `DELETE FROM site_settings`). Rolling back will raise ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration, and even a manual reverse can't restore the deleted `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` setting rows. This should be split into `up`/`down` with an explicit, safe down (or acknowledge irreversibility).

No foreign key or cleanup for category_id

`category_id` is `null: false` but has no foreign key, and the `EmbeddableHost` model has no `belongs_to` presence validation or dependent handling. Deleting a category leaves dangling `embeddable_hosts.category_id` values; `TopicEmbed.import` will then create topics pointing at a nonexistent category (PostCreator is given the stale id, and `ensure_topic_has_a_category` won't fix it since the id isn't nil), and the admin UI renders a missing category badge. Add a FK and/or handle category deletion.

show always renders JSON, so direct navigation/refresh to /admin/customize/embedding breaks

`show` unconditionally calls `render_serialized(...)`, which renders JSON for every format. The sibling customize pages (permalinks, colors, emojis, site texts) respond with an HTML page that boots the Ember admin app for non-XHR requests; this controller (and its missing view template) does not. Opening or refreshing `https://site/admin/customize/embedding` directly in a browser returns a raw JSON payload instead of the admin UI. Add `respond_to`/`format.html` handling plus the blank HTML view like the other admin customize controllers.

No uniqueness constraint on host

Neither the model nor the migration enforces uniqueness of `host`. The admin UI lets the same host be added multiple times with different categories, and `record_for_host` uses `.first`, so which category an embedded topic lands in becomes nondeterministic. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and a unique index (the migration's data copy should also dedupe).

Host validation regex rejects legitimate TLDs longer than 5 characters

The regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` for the final label, so valid domains like `example.technology`, `example.international` or `example.museum` fail validation and can't be added as embedding hosts. The old free-text setting imposed no such restriction, so this is a new, undocumented limitation.

Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it claims

`Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer consults embeddable hosts at all. The spec still asserts that it "is false if embeddable_host is blank", but it passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false — it would pass identically if a host existed, so it guards nothing about the removed condition. The example should be renamed/rewritten to reflect the new contract (or removed).

New admin endpoints have no request specs

The specs for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (and `Admin::EmbeddingController`) only assert the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. All the actual behavior added in this PR — creating/updating a host, the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` when category is blank, validation errors, unknown-id handling, destroy, and the embedding show payload — is completely untested, which is how the nil-record and nil-param crashes slip through.

Controller specs bypass the router, so the test still passes — and for the same reason none of the add_members/remove_member specs detect that the actual routes supply the group id as `params[:id]` while the controller requires `params[:group_id]` (which makes the feature fail with a 400 in production). true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is off by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit

`totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For e.g. 100 members with limit 50 this returns 3, although only 2 pages exist (the correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`). Because `showingLast` compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the "next" button stays enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets offset = user_count, and the server returns an empty list, so the admin lands on a phantom empty page (e.g. "3/3" with no members). This affects every group whose member count is an exact multiple of 50.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same off-by-one bug in the `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, and both even use the same example (100 users, limit 50 resulting in 3 pages instead of 2).

true_positives.golden_comment: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] but the routes only provide params[:id]

The new routes in config/routes.rb (lines 49-50) are declared as bare `delete "members"` / `put "members"` inside `resources :groups`, which Rails turns into member routes of the form `/admin/groups/:id/members` — the group id arrives in `params[:id]`. However `add_members` (line 66) and `remove_member` (line 85) do `params.require(:group_id)`, and the Ember client (discourse/models/group.js removeMember/addMembers) puts the id only in the URL path, sending only `user_id`/`usernames` in the body. As a result every real request to add or remove a member raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns a 400, so both features are completely broken in production. The controller specs don't catch this because they bypass the router and inject `group_id` directly. false_positives.candidate:
Public group members list is now truncated to 50 with no pagination UI

Previously `members` returned all members for non-automatic groups and only applied a limit (default 200) to automatic ones. The new code applies `limit` (default 50) to every group. The public group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 calls findMembers with the model's default limit of 50, and discourse/templates/group/members.hbs has no next/previous controls) therefore now shows only the first 50 members of any larger group, with no way for users to see the rest — a regression from the previous behavior. Pagination support (or a higher cap) is needed on the public page, not just the admin page.

{{#unless automatic}} checks the member's automatic flag, so the remove link always renders

This template is rendered as the itemView of `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` in admin/templates/group.hbs, so its context is the member (a User), not the group. Users have no `automatic` property, so `automatic` is undefined and the `{{#unless automatic}}` guard always passes — the remove (×) link is rendered for members of automatic groups too. Clicking it triggers Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, which correctly rejects the request with a 422 (`can_not_modify_automatic`), and the client's `removeMember` action has no error handling, so the admin just gets a confusing failure. The template needs the group's flag (e.g. via the parent view/controller) instead of resolving `automatic` on the member.

limit parameter on public members endpoint is unbounded

`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any value with no maximum, and this endpoint is reachable by any user who can see the group. A request with `limit=1000000` will load and serialize that many users in one request. The old code had the same flaw but only for automatic groups; it now applies to all groups. Clamp the limit (e.g. `[[limit, 200].min, 1].max`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
match_count is incremented twice per failed signup because should_block? has a side effect inside validation

BlockedEmail.should_block? writes to the database (match_count += 1, last_match_at = now, save) every time it runs, and it is invoked from EmailValidator, i.e. from user validation. UsersController#create (app/controllers/users_controller.rb) calls user.valid? on line 168 and then user.save on line 172, both of which run the full validation suite, so a single signup attempt with a blocked email increments match_count by 2 and updates last_match_at twice. Any other code path that calls valid? before save does the same. The match_count/last_match_at statistics (whose purpose is explicitly described in the specs) will therefore be wrong for the primary flow they were built for. The stats update should be separated from validation (e.g. done once in the controller when a block actually rejects the signup) or made idempotent per request. The specs call should_block? directly, so they never exercise this double-run.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same core problem: the `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (or `should_block_email?`) predicate method has a database write side effect (updating statistics like `match_count` and `last_match_at`) during a read/check operation. The candidate goes further to explain a concrete bug caused by this side effect (double incrementing during validation), which reinforces the exact concern raised in the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so blocks are trivially bypassed by changing letter case

BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match lookup: BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. Nothing downcases the user's email before validation — User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] verbatim and the User model never normalizes case (unlike change_email, which uses Email.downcase). A blocked address spammer@example.com will therefore not match Spammer@example.com or SPAMMER@EXAMPLE.COM, letting a blocked user register by simply varying case. The unique index added in the migration is case-sensitive as well, so variants can coexist in the table. The lookup should compare downcased emails (and ideally the column should be normalized on write).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same vulnerability as the golden comment: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a case-sensitive lookup, allowing blocked users to bypass the check by changing the casing of their email address.

false_positives.candidate:
Any server email error (e.g. 'has already been taken') marks the address as rejected and mislabels it invalid

On account-creation failure the client pushes result.values.email into rejectedEmails whenever result.errors.email exists, and emailValidation then reports I18n.t('user.email.invalid') for that address. But errors.email is present for any email validation failure, not just blocking — most commonly the uniqueness validation (User validates :email, uniqueness: true), which produces 'has already been taken'. A user whose signup failed because the email is already registered (or who hits the ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid duplicate race after a retry) will see 'email is invalid' from then on and will be unable to re-validate that address for the rest of the session, with no hint that the real problem is a duplicate. The client should only track emails rejected specifically by the blocked-email rule (e.g. a dedicated error code from the server), not any email error.

match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write and record.save can silently fail

should_block? loads the record, does record.match_count += 1, then record.save. Two concurrent signup attempts against the same blocked email both read the same match_count and one increment is lost. Additionally, the return value of record.save is ignored, so if the save fails (e.g. a validation error from a concurrent change) the statistics are silently dropped while the block decision still proceeds. Use an atomic update (e.g. update_counters or UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1) for the stats bump.

Blocked-email match statistics are not recorded when another email validation already failed

The blocked check is gated on record.errors[attribute].blank?, so BlockedEmail.should_block? is never called if the email already has an error from the presence/uniqueness validators (which run before this one in User) or from the domain whitelist/blacklist check above. That means a signup attempt using a blocked email that also trips another rule — for example re-registering an email that is both blocked and already taken — leaves no trace in match_count or last_match_at, undercounting abuse attempts. If the gate exists only to avoid duplicate error messages, the stats recording should still happen and only the errors.add should be conditional.

change_email does not check the blocked list before sending the authorization email

UsersController#change_email only checks that the new email is not already in use, then creates an email token and enqueues the authorize_email message. A logged-in user can therefore request an email change to a blocked address and have the system send mail to it; the block is only (silently) enforced later if EmailToken.confirm saves the user and triggers the model validation, at which point the email change fails with no feedback to the user. The blocked check should also run in change_email so the request is rejected up front with a clear error.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
float: right on .small-action button is dead because the container is now flexbox

This PR makes .small-action a flex container (@include flexbox() at the top of the rule), but the nested button still relies on `float: right` for its position. The float property has no effect on flex items, so the button rendered in small-action posts (e.g. the staff edit/action button on 'topic closed'-style posts) will no longer be pinned to the right edge of the row — it will be laid out immediately after .small-action-desc, because neither the button nor .small-action-desc has margin-left: auto or flex-grow to push it right. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button (or let .small-action-desc grow) and remove the now-inert float.

margin-left: auto used to right-align .panel does not work in the legacy box syntax the flexbox() mixin emits

.panel lost `float: right` and is now pushed to the right edge solely by `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container .contents. The flexbox() mixin applied to .contents also emits the 2009-syntax `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` fallbacks, and the 2009 flexbox model does not support auto margins (they compute to 0). So in exactly the legacy browsers those prefixes exist for, the header icon panel will sit immediately after the title instead of at the right edge — a regression from the previous float-based layout, which worked everywhere. Either drop the 2009 display fallbacks or provide a fallback (e.g. keep a float on .panel, or use -webkit-box-pack on the container).

align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align, inconsistent with the other new flexbox mixins

The new align-items mixin emits -webkit-box-align, -ms-flex-align and modern declarations but no -moz-box-align. Its sibling mixins flexbox() and order() both include the 2009 Mozilla syntax (-moz-box, -moz-box-ordinal-group), so on Gecko versions that only implement the legacy box model, an element using these mixins becomes a -moz-box with ordering applied while the requested alignment (center in the header/small-action, baseline on category bullets) is silently ignored — the mixin half-works in exactly the engines it claims to support. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` for consistency (the 2009 spec accepts start/end/center/baseline/stretch).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is dead code — missing '?' so AMS never calls it

ActiveModelSerializers decides whether to serialize an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark), as used everywhere else in this file (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`, etc.). The added method is named `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always included in the payload — serialized as explicit null for users who have no website — instead of being omitted when `website` is blank. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (or, better, add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` as noted in the other finding, which also defines the include predicate).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies the main problem in the golden comment: `include_website_name` is missing the required `?` suffix expected by ActiveModelSerializers for conditional attribute inclusion. Although the golden comment also mentions a secondary issue about string concatenation, the core bug is matched.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name bypasses the TL0/anonymous restriction that hides website

The serializer deliberately hides `website` (along with bio, location, etc.) for trust-level-0 users viewed by anonymous visitors via the `untrusted_attributes` mechanism (`include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`). The new `website_name` attribute is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list, and its value is derived directly from `object.user_profile.website`, so anonymous visitors now receive `website_name` (the website's host, plus full path when it matches the instance domain) in the JSON for TL0 users even though `website` itself is withheld. This defeats the anti-spam purpose of restricting those fields. The existing spec 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' will not catch this because `website_name` isn't in its attribute list either. Fix by adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or checking `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` in its include guard) and extend the spec to cover it.

Websites Ruby's URI parser rejects (e.g. IDN/Unicode domains) disappear from the profile entirely

`URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for any stored website that Ruby's ASCII-only URI parser cannot handle, such as non-ASCII/IDN domains. `website_name` then returns nil, and since the template renders the globe icon and link only inside `{{#if model.website_name}}`, the user's website stops being displayed on their profile at all. The previous client-side code (`website.split("/")[2]`) still displayed the domain for such URLs, so this is a regression for affected users. Consider falling back to the raw `website` string when URI parsing fails instead of returning nil.

No test for the sibling-subdomain branch of website_name

The most complex branch of `website_name` — the `elsif` that compares parent domains when website and instance hosts have equal label depth greater than 2 (e.g. show the full path for `www.example.com` on a `forum.example.com` instance, but only the host for `www.other.com`) — has no test coverage. The three added examples only exercise the equal-host case and the website-domain-is-parent case, so a regression in the parent-domain comparison would not be caught.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Unescaped URL interpolated into href attribute of posts rendered as raw HTML TopicEmbed.import appends an 'Imported from' footer built as "#{url}" with the URL inserted unescaped. The only validation is that the URL starts with http(s)://; a single quote is a valid URI character, so a feed item link or an embed URL like http://host/page'onmouseover='alert(1) breaks out of the href attribute and injects arbitrary attributes/markup into the post body. Because these posts are created with cook_method raw_html, Post#cook returns the raw string with no sanitization, and the embed view renders it via `raw post.cooked` (and the main site renders cooked verbatim), this becomes stored XSS on the forum origin for everyone who views the imported topic or embed. Escape the URL (e.g. ERB::Util.html_escape) before interpolating it into the attribute.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment identifies two issues in TopicEmbed.import: a NoMethodError when contents is nil, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in generated HTML. The candidate issue specifically and accurately identifies the XSS vulnerability caused by unescaped URL interpolation in TopicEmbed.import.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed items without content crash the polling job permanently

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content element. With simple-rss, RSS 2.0 items only expose #content when the feed includes <content:encoded>; a large number of feeds carry only <description>, and Atom entries may omit content too. One such item raises out of the each loop, aborting the whole poll (the job has retry: false), and since items are processed in feed order the same item crashes the job again on every hourly run, so no later items are ever imported. Fall back to i.description / to_s and wrap per-item processing so one bad item cannot kill the entire feed poll.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: calling `i.content.scrub` will raise an error (nil pointer / NoMethodError) when an RSS item does not have a `content` field, and both suggest falling back to `i.description`.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
request.referer injected into a JavaScript string with only HTML escaping

The embed layout interpolates request.referer directly into a single-quoted JS string: parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>'). ERB output is HTML-escaped, which is the wrong escaping context for a JavaScript string — and in the Rails 3 boot mode this repo still supports, ERB's html_escape does not escape single quotes at all. A request to /embed/best with a Referer such as http://<embeddable-host>/';alert(1);// passes the ensure_embeddable host check (a single quote and semicolons are legal characters in a URI path) and breaks out of the JS string, executing arbitrary script inside the iframe on the forum's own origin. Use request.referer.to_json (or escape_javascript) when building the targetOrigin string.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same XSS vulnerability: `request.referer` is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string without proper JavaScript escaping, allowing arbitrary script execution.

false_positives.candidate:
raw_html cook method renders remotely fetched content with zero sanitization

Post#cook now returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing PrettyText's sanitizer entirely. The content stored in these posts comes from remote sources: feed items via PollFeed (no filtering at all) and arbitrary pages on the embeddable host via TopicRetriever/import_remote (ruby-readability whitelists tags/attributes but still passes through href/src values such as javascript: URLs). Any script, event handler, or javascript: link in the source HTML is rendered verbatim on topic pages, in the embed iframe on the forum origin, in email digests, etc. Additionally, PostCreator now honors opts[:cook_method] for every caller (lib/post_creator.rb setup_post) — if request parameters ever flow into PostCreator opts, any user could create unsanitized raw-HTML posts, so this must be guarded against.

TopicEmbed row is created even when PostCreator rolled the post back, leaving a dangling reference

import only checks `if post.present?` before calling TopicEmbed.create!, but PostCreator#create returns the unsaved post object (with errors) when creation fails — for example when rollback_if_host_spam_detected fires, which happens for a trust-level-0 embed user importing an article that links several times to the same host (newuser_spam_host_threshold). In that case the inner Post transaction rolls back the topic and post inserts, but TopicEmbed.create! still commits a row whose topic_id/post_id point at records that no longer exist. Every subsequent /embed/best request for that URL then finds the dead topic_id and TopicView raises not-found/invalid-access, so the embed for that URL is permanently broken and the import is never retried. Check post.persisted? / post.errors.empty? instead of post.present?.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs Both the and rewriting treat any value starting with '/' as root-relative and rewrite it to prefix + path. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/image.png (common in feeds and CMS output) also start with '/', so they are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/image.png, breaking the link or image. Values starting with '//' should be left alone.

Unauthenticated endpoint enqueues unbounded outbound-fetch jobs

Any GET to /embed/best whose Referer host matches embeddable_host (a header trivially forged by non-browser clients) and that carries a previously unseen embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, which performs an outbound HTTP fetch of that URL. The only throttle is a 60-second redis key per URL inside the job, so an attacker can enqueue unlimited jobs simply by varying the URL — exhausting sidekiq workers and directing a flood of fetches at the configured embeddable host. There should be a global or per-IP rate limit before enqueuing retrieval work.

Every new embed URL runs a full synchronous feed poll

When feed_polling_enabled? is on, perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed inline for each retrieval before falling back to direct HTTP fetch. The retrieval throttle is keyed per embed URL, so N distinct new embed URLs cause N full feed downloads/parses (and a re-import/revision pass over every feed item) inside RetrieveTopic jobs. The unused feed_key method on PollFeed suggests a per-feed throttle was intended but never wired up.

Missing Referer hard-fails embedding for legitimate visitors

ensure_embeddable raises Discourse::InvalidAccess when request.referer is blank. Visitors using referer-stripping privacy extensions, behind referer-removing proxies, or on an HTTPS page embedding an HTTP forum (browsers omit Referer on the HTTPS→HTTP downgrade) will get an error instead of the comment embed. The check only needs to reject referers from foreign hosts; a blank referer could be treated as allowed so these users still see comments.

Disqus import no longer preserves the thread's original creation date

Before this change the topic-opening post was created with created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]); the new code path calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]), which provides no way to pass created_at, so every imported thread's opening post is timestamped at import time. Imported forums lose their original chronology (topic ordering, 'x days ago' dates, digest ordering). Add a created_at option to import/import_remote and pass the thread date through.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

self.downsize is defined twice; the 4-argument version is dead and old callers silently misbehave

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Client upload size check hardcodes 10MB for all types, ignoring the per-type site settings

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Large animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame

The downsize call passes `tempfile.path` as `from`, and `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects the animated (gifsicle) code path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Upload tempfiles created by Rack (and the API download tempfile) do not carry the original file extension, so for normal composer uploads this check is always false and a large animated GIF is processed by `convert from[0] ...`, whose `[0]` selects only the first frame and writes a static image back over the user's original file — the animation is silently destroyed even when `allow_animation` is enabled. false_positives.candidate: Topic unsubscribe mutates user state via an unprotected GET request The new `topics#unsubscribe` action is routed as `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`, and it changes the current user's TopicUser notification level (demoting tracking/watching to regular, or muting) as a side effect of a plain GET. Concretely: an attacker can embed `` in a post, PM, or external page and every logged-in viewer gets muted/unsubscribed from topic 123. Additionally, corporate email gateways and security link-scanners that fetch URLs found in incoming mail will trigger the unsubscribe without the user ever clicking. Because the mutation runs on every GET of the unsubscribe URL, repeating the request keeps changing the user's state: a watching user is demoted to regular on first load and then fully muted if they simply refresh the confirmation page (or hit back/forward, or a prefetcher re-fetches the link). Discourse intercepts clicks on same-origin links (for example an unsubscribe URL posted inside a topic or PM) and transitions client-side without a server round-trip, so a user arriving that way sees a message asserting they were unsubscribed when nothing changed — the opposite result from opening the same URL in a new tab, which does unsubscribe them. true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

The intent was evidently `.isSame()` to detect zero-length overrides (start == end, i.e. a fully blocked day). As written, blocked-day detection falls through to the other conditions, which happen to reject most slots but let a slot starting exactly at the override start pass, and the dead branch misleads anyone maintaining this logic.

A matching date override should only bypass the working-hours check; the busy/busy-calendar check must still run.

The new working-hours guard only rejects a slot when it finds a workingHour entry whose `days` includes the slot's weekday AND the slot is outside that entry's window. If the fixed host has no availability row for that weekday (e.g. they don't work weekends), `workingHours.find(...)` returns undefined, the guard passes, and only busy times are checked. For a round-robin event, slots generated from another (non-fixed) host's schedule on the fixed host's day off are therefore still offered — exactly the kind of over-booking this PR is meant to prevent. A weekday with no matching working-hours entry should be treated as unavailable.

Slots inside one of several same-day override windows are rejected

The `dateOverrides.find(...)` at line 106 returns truthy as soon as ANY override on the slot's date does not contain the slot (slot ends at/before that override's start, or starts after its end). When a host has multiple override windows on the same day (e.g. 09:00–11:00 and 14:00–16:00), a slot at 10:00 is inside the first window but 'outside' the second, so find() returns the second override and the function returns false — the slot is hidden even though the host is available. The slot should be considered covered if it fits inside ANY of that day's override windows. Additionally the boundary is off by one: `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)` is strict, so a slot starting exactly at an override's end is treated as inside the override and returned as available although it lies outside every window.

The PR's headline change — applying fixed hosts' date overrides and working hours in checkIfIsAvailable for round-robin events (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts) — is only covered by manual testing steps. The single added test exercises a personal event's slot generation with a different invitee timezone. The new checkIfIsAvailable logic has several interacting branches (override match, blocked day, working-hours bounds, busy times) and contains regressions a test would catch, e.g. a fixed host with a date override plus a conflicting existing booking is currently shown as available. A round-robin scenario with a fixed host who has a date override and a busy period on that day should be added.

The invitee-local override start/end are computed as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute').hour() * 60 + .minute()`. If applying `offset` (invitee offset minus organizer offset) pushes the time across midnight — e.g. an 00:30–02:00 override for an Asia/Kolkata host viewed by a UTC-4 invitee becomes 09:30 the previous day — `.hour()/.minute()` keep only the time-of-day and the day shift is lost. Combined with the `activeOverrides` filter, which matches overrides by the organizer-local date against the invitee's day, such overrides produce slots at the wrong time on the wrong day instead of on the adjacent invitee day.

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` creates the Dayjs in the server's local timezone (no `.utc()`), while the slot side `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` is in UTC mode. Relatedly, when `organizerTimeZone` is undefined the offset silently falls back to 0, treating the override's wall-clock times as UTC.

`TimeRange.timeZone` was added as optional, but the conversion does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` unconditionally and never falls back to the `organizerTimeZone` parameter that getSlots already receives. The corrupted records are then sorted by the wrong `timestamp` and sent to Seer as the error context for the replay summary, so the summary can cite the wrong errors in the wrong chronological positions. The function already computes `node_ids`; it should look up each event explicitly (e.g. `events.get(node_id)` for each `(error_id, node_id)` pair) instead of relying on `.values()` ordering.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi dictionary values align with input IDs, causing incorrect pairings when ordering differs or events are missing.

false_positives.candidate:
Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed, replayable forever, and cannot be removed

With this PR a recovery-code credential can now live in an external user storage, but the 'single use' semantics of recovery codes are lost on that path. For locally stored codes, RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid() marks the used code as consumed so it cannot be replayed and the next login asks for the next unused code. For a federated credential, validation is delegated to the storage's CredentialInputValidator.isValid() (a read-only boolean check, see BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid) and nothing ever marks a code as used, so the credential reconstructed from the storage always shows all 12 codes as unused. Consequences: (1) every recovery code of a storage-backed user stays valid indefinitely and can be replayed by anyone who observed it once; (2) the login form always asks for code #1, because RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() on an all-unused credential, so code rotation never happens; (3) the cleanup here at lines 85-88 calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id), which only removes credentials from Keycloak's own store — the CredentialInputUpdater SPI has no remove-by-id operation for external storages — so even an exhausted federated credential would silently never be deleted (likewise, admin delete/disable of such a credential is a no-op in the sample provider). The new test BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.enterRecoveryCodes actually bakes in the always-code-#0 behavior rather than detecting it. Before merging, used-code state should be pushed back to the storage (e.g., via CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential after a successful validation) or the limitation explicitly documented and tested.

Raw recovery codes are sent to and persisted in user storage as plaintext JSON

In CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, when the credential is delegated to a user storage, the raw, unhashed recovery codes are serialized (JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes) at line 119) and passed to CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential as the UserCredentialModel challenge response, so the external store persists all 12 valid codes in plaintext JSON. When the same credential is created locally (line 129), only SHA-512 hashes are stored, because RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues hashes each code via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode. Consequence: for storage-backed users, anyone with read access to the external store (database, backups, logs) immediately obtains working recovery codes that bypass the second factor entirely — a weaker protection level than Keycloak's own store provides for the identical data. The sample provider BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage mirrors this by storing the plaintext JSON and comparing the presented code in cleartext. The hashed credential data (credentialModel.getCredentialData()) could be sent to the storage instead, with validators hashing the presented code via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode before comparing, so both storage paths keep only hashes.

User label and original generation timestamp are dropped when recovery codes go to user storage

createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the UserCredentialModel sent to the user storage with only the JSON array of codes; the generatedUserLabel (collected from the setup form and applied to the locally created credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues) and the generatedAt timestamp are never transmitted. The sample storage (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential, recovery-codes branch) therefore stores createdDate = write time and userLabel = null. Consequence: the same setup flow produces different credential metadata depending on where the credential lands — the label the user assigned is silently lost for storage-backed users and createdDate no longer reflects when the codes were generated, which shows up incorrectly in the account console and breaks parity between the two paths. The label and generation time should be included in the payload sent to CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

Any automation written against the previous preview that branches on exit code 4 to decide that a recreate upgrade is required will now misinterpret that case: a 'recreate required' result returns 3 (which such a script would treat as an unknown error), and a 'feature disabled' result returns 4 (which it would treat as 'recreate required', potentially triggering an unnecessary full shutdown and downtime). The three overrides should include canManage(client) (or include the MANAGE scope in the evaluated scopes, as the Users V2 implementation does via varargs).

init() creates the schema scopes and the all-type resources only when the admin-permissions client does not exist yet, and returns immediately if it does. Realms that enabled admin permissions (V2) before this change already have that client, so they never get the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) or the "Clients" resource-type resource. In such realms, creating a Clients permission fails in getOrCreateResource with ModelException("No scopes found.") when it looks up the missing scopes, and permission evaluation falls into the getResourceTypeResource() == null path in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission. A migration or repair step that adds newly introduced scopes and resource-type resources to existing admin-permissions resource servers is needed.

getResourceName has no Clients branch and returns null display names for Clients resources

getResourceName only resolves display names for the Users resource type and otherwise falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Resources created for the admin-permissions schema (the all-type "Clients" resource and per-client resources) never have a display name set, so permission/resource representations for Clients resources come back with null names, and there is no "All clients" equivalent of the existing "All users" label. Add a CLIENTS branch that resolves the client (e.g., returning its clientId) for per-client resources and "All clients" for the type resource.

Null 'Groups' type resource is dereferenced; no upgrade path creates it for realms that already enabled admin permissions

In hasPermission(), when no per-group resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Groups") and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).getId() semantics — getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource server has no resource named "Groups", and findByResource(server, null) NPEs inside the store, producing a 500 on any group admin endpoint (group list, view, manage checks). Any existing compiled implementation used with the newer keycloak-common will fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` as soon as `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider()` sorts via `CryptoProvider::order`, and any source implementation stops compiling until it implements the method. true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same backward-compatibility issue: adding abstract order() to CryptoProvider breaks existing implementations. The candidate further explains the source and runtime failures and suggests a default method.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-order crypto providers are now silently picked by classpath order instead of failing fast

detectProvider() previously threw IllegalStateException("Multiple crypto providers loaded... Make sure only one cryptoProvider available on the classpath") whenever more than one CryptoProvider was found. Now it sorts by order() and unconditionally takes the first entry. Because DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, a misconfigured classpath containing two of them — exactly the situation the old exception guarded against — no longer fails: one provider is silently chosen based on ServiceLoader/classpath ordering, which can vary between environments, and the only trace is a debug-level "Ignored crypto providers" message. The functional core of this PR is that AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered via META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider and is selected by CryptoIntegration only when no higher-order provider is present (DefaultCryptoProvider et al. use order 200, this one 100). The added test instantiates `new AuthzClientCryptoProvider()` directly, so a broken or missing service registration file, or an order() value that wins/loses incorrectly against DefaultCryptoProvider, would not be caught by anything. A test that loads providers through ServiceLoader/CryptoIntegration — e.g. asserting AuthzClientCryptoProvider is discoverable on its own and that DefaultCryptoProvider still wins when both are on the classpath — would cover the mechanism the PR actually introduces.

If a group deletion throws, the polling thread spins forever for the rest of the JVM lifetime

deletedAll.set(true) on line 155 is only reached if every managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove() call in the preceding forEach succeeds. If any deletion throws (which is exactly the kind of failure this concurrency test is probing for), the flag is never set and the non-daemon reader thread keeps looping while (!deletedAll.get()) indefinitely, firing REST calls in a tight no-sleep loop and appending every resulting exception to the unbounded CopyOnWriteArrayList caughtExceptions. The PR fixes getSubGroupsCount() for the case where the group is concurrently deleted (modelSupplier.get() returns null), but the three getSubGroupsStream overloads directly above it (lines 256, 262, and 268) still dereference the supplier result without a null check: return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...).
